calibration_source: USGS HVO measurements + LANDFIRE basalt spectra + ARRI ALEXA reference plates from Hawaii Volcanoes NP / Eyjafjallajökull / Mount St. Helens

aaa_targets.intent: Late-stage active stratovolcano caldera, post-eruption ashfall still settling, sub-aerial lava lake at floor, dark fantasy mood (low key, high contrast, smoke-dimmed sun).

fresh_basalt_rock.notes: Real basalt measures 5-7% reflectance (USGS spectral library, sample bas-1). Common AAA bug: artists set 0.018 (charcoal value) which crushes blacks under volumetric haze. Floor is 0.05; never go below.

weathered_basalt.notes: Sun/rain-weathered basalt picks up ~2% from oxidation patina. Slightly warmer due to iron oxide bloom.

volcanic_ash_tephra_dry.notes: Dry fresh tephra reads as medium-dark grey, NOT white. Mt. St. Helens 1980 deposits measured 14-18% reflectance. White ash is a film/TV cliché — real ash is dark grey unless it is hydrated rhyolitic pumice.

volcanic_ash_wet.notes: Rain-soaked ash drops ~50% in luminance. Important for rain shaders / wetness masks.

cooled_lava_crust_pahoehoe.notes: Pahoehoe (smooth, ropy) crust is the darkest natural surface in the scene. Slightly glossy from glassy quench skin. Never raise above 0.05 — destroys the silhouette read against ash.

cooled_lava_crust_aa.notes: A'a (rough clinker) is slightly more reflective than pahoehoe due to micro-faceting.

obsidian.notes: Volcanic glass. Critical: keep rough <0.10 or it loses the mirror quality. Iridescence layer (rainbow sheen) is what sells obsidian vs plain black rock.

active_lava_surface.notes: Active lava lake surface (Halemaʻumaʻu, Kīlauea) measures ~1100°C = 1373K = blackbody peak in deep orange. Surface luminance 8000-15000 cd/m2 depending on crust coverage. Use 12000 for partial-crust default. Pure exposed magma at fountain spike: 80000 cd/m2.

incandescent_lava_crack.notes: Bright cracks between cooled crust plates. Higher temperature than bulk surface (insulating crust pushes exposed cracks hotter).

sulfur_deposit.notes: Native sulfur fumarole crystals — yellow-green, only material in the scene above 0.3 albedo. Use sparingly to give the eye a chromatic anchor.

scoria_red.notes: Oxidized red cinder — appears in cinder cone flanks. Hematite-rich, warm tone.

charred_wood.notes: Carbonized tree bark. Real char is darker than 'black' paint.

ash_dusted_overlay.notes: Dust mask overlay — applied to upward-facing surfaces only. Drives the 'powdered with grey' AAA look. Thickness driven by displacement noise.

sun.notes: Heavy volcanic aerosol (PM2.5 > 200 ug/m3) attenuates direct sun by 6.5x. Color shifts orange-red as blue scatters out (Rayleigh + Mie). 4200K is post-eruption Pinatubo measured value. Soft shadows (4-5 deg apparent disc) because sun is diffused through ash, not a point source.

sky_dome.notes: Volcanic sky is BROWN-ORANGE near horizon, dim purple-grey at zenith. NOT blue. Ambient drops ~75% vs clear day. This is what kills naive Nishita setups — they render as bright daylight blue.

lava_fill_lights.notes: Lava is the ONLY warm chromatic source in the scene. Distance falloff matters more than peak intensity — aim for spill that reaches mid-rim. Use mesh-emission area lights (NOT point lights — point lights miss occlusion and create wrong silhouettes on rim rocks).

fumarole_rim_glow.notes: Sulfurous fumarole steam picks up nearby lava bounce. Subtle warm glow inside the steam volumes.

atmosphere.haze_color_description: Warm brown-grey, NOT cool blue. Volcanic ash PM2.5 + SO2 absorbs blue, scatters red-orange.
atmosphere.asymmetry_notes: Strong forward-scattering — ash is large compared to wavelength. Halo around sun, dark backlit silhouettes.
atmosphere.notes: Visibility 0.5-2 km horizontal. This is what makes the silhouette of the far rim read — it MUST fade into haze, not remain crisp.

bloom.notes: Bloom should ONLY trigger on lava/incandescent surfaces. If bloom hits the sky disc you have it set wrong.

post_processing.notes: Cycles + AgX is the current Blender-native AAA path. ACES is acceptable fallback. Never use Filmic Standard — it crushes the lava highlights.

silhouette.comment: The caldera rim must read as a clear dark band against the orange-grey sky at any time of day. If contrast < 6.0, the silhouette is mush — re-check sky brightness or rim albedo.

depth_cues.near_field_0_50m: Crisp microdetail, full albedo readable, ash dust on top faces, lava cracks fully chromatic.
depth_cues.mid_field_50_300m: Albedo desaturates ~30%, micro-detail blends, lava becomes the dominant chromatic anchor.
depth_cues.far_field_300_2000m: Silhouette only, fully desaturated, haze tint dominates, lava reads as warm point or line.
depth_cues.comment: Aerial perspective in volcanic conditions is 3-4x stronger than clear-day baseline. Distant rim should be ~80% haze color.

color_palette_dominance.comment: Histogram should be bimodal: one cluster in deep blacks (basalt+lava crust), one in warm midtones (ash+haze), with a tiny fire-orange spike. If the histogram is flat or has a blue peak, lighting is wrong.

contrast_targets.comment: Lava-to-shadow is 11 stops — this is what mandates 14+ stop HDR pipeline. SDR clipping is unacceptable.

geological_realism_checklist: Caldera rim higher than caldera floor (always — never inverted).
Lava channels follow steepest descent — NEVER cross contour lines.
Cinder cones have slope angles 30-33 deg (angle of repose for scoria).
Pahoehoe near vent, transitions to a'a downstream as it cools.
Ash mantles top-facing surfaces only (Y+ normal threshold).
Tree skeletons concentrate downwind of vent (pyroclastic flow direction).
No vegetation in inner caldera (heat zone ~150m radius from vent).
Fumarole vents at fault lines / rim cracks, not random.

negative_examples: Cartoon volcano red rocks bright orange — TOO SATURATED, NOT REALISTIC
Hollywood 'snowy ash' white powder volcano — WRONG, ash is dark grey
Blue-sky daytime volcano — wrong mood for active eruption scene

asset_overrides.comment: Catch-all guardrail: any procedural fallback material outside [0.05, 0.65] linear luminance is rejected as physically implausible for this scene.
